units.text: INT. FAN - CONTINUOUS
Aside .

Berwick and I told her that didn’t matter much, as the lady in question must have an extremely fine figure. You should have seen Arabella’s expression! . . . But, look here, dear boy. I don’t know what to do about Mrs. Erlynne. Egad! I might be married to her; she treats me with such demmed indifference. She’s deuced clever, too! She explains everything. Egad! she explains you. She has got any amount of explanations for you—and all of them different.
units.name: LORD AUGUSTUS

units.text: No explanations are necessary about my friendship with Mrs. Erlynne.
units.name: LORD WINDERMERE

units.text: Hem! Well, look here, dear old fellow. Do you think she will ever get into this demmed thing called Society? Would you introduce her to your wife? No use beating about the confounded bush. Would you do that?
units.name: LORD AUGUSTUS

units.text: Mrs. Erlynne is coming here to-night.
units.name: LORD WINDERMERE

units.text: Your wife has sent her a card?
units.name: LORD AUGUSTUS

units.text: Mrs. Erlynne has received a card.
units.name: LORD WINDERMERE

units.text: Then she’s all right, dear boy. But why didn’t you tell me that before? It would have saved me a heap of worry and demmed misunderstandings!
units.name: LORD AUGUSTUS

units.text: LADY AGATHA and MR. HOPPER cross and exit on terrace L.U.E.
Mr. Cecil Graham!
units.name: PARKER

units.text: Enter MR. CECIL GRAHAM.
Bows to LADY WINDERMERE, passes over and shakes hands with LORD WINDERMERE.

Good evening, Arthur. Why don’t you ask me how I am? I like people to ask me how I am. It shows a wide-spread interest in my health. Now, to-night I am not at all well. Been dining with my people. Wonder why it is one’s people are always so tedious? My father would talk morality after dinner. I told him he was old enough to know better. But my experience is that as soon as people are old enough to know better, they don’t know anything at all. Hallo, Tuppy! Hear you’re going to be married again; thought you were tired of that game.
units.name: CECIL GRAHAM

units.text: You’re excessively trivial, my dear boy, excessively trivial!
units.name: LORD AUGUSTUS

units.text: By the way, Tuppy, which is it? Have you been twice married and once divorced, or twice divorced and once married? I say you’ve been twice divorced and once married. It seems so much more probable.
units.name: CECIL GRAHAM

units.text: I have a very bad memory. I really don’t remember which.
units.name: LORD AUGUSTUS

units.text: Moves away R.
Lord Windermere, I’ve something most particular to ask you.
units.name: LADY PLYMDALE

units.text: I am afraid—if you will excuse me—I must join my wife.
units.name: LORD WINDERMERE

units.text: Oh, you mustn’t dream of such a thing. It’s most dangerous nowadays for a husband to pay any attention to his wife in public. It always makes people think that he beats her when they’re alone. The world has grown so suspicious of anything that looks like a happy married life. But I’ll tell you what it is at supper.
units.name: LADY PLYMDALE

units.text: Moves towards door of ball-room .
Margaret! I must speak to you.
units.name: LORD WINDERMERE

units.text: Will you hold my fan for me, Lord Darlington? Thanks.
units.name: LADY WINDERMERE

units.text: Comes down to him .
Crossing to her .
Margaret, what you said before dinner was, of course, impossible?
units.name: LORD WINDERMERE

units.text: That woman is not coming here to-night!
units.name: LADY WINDERMERE

units.text: R.C.
Mrs. Erlynne is coming here, and if you in any way annoy or wound her, you will bring shame and sorrow on us both. Remember that! Ah, Margaret! only trust me! A wife should trust her husband!
units.name: LORD WINDERMERE

units.text: London is full of women who trust their husbands. One can always recognise them. They look so thoroughly unhappy. I am not going to be one of them.
units.name: LADY WINDERMERE

units.text: Moves up .
Lord Darlington, will you give me back my fan, please? Thanks. . . . A useful thing a fan, isn’t it? . . . I want a friend to-night, Lord Darlington: I didn’t know I would want one so soon.
units.name: LADY WINDERMERE

units.text: Lady Windermere! I knew the time would come some day; but why to-night?
units.name: LORD DARLINGTON

units.text: I will tell her. I must. It would be terrible if there were any scene. Margaret . . .
units.name: LORD WINDERMERE

units.text: Mrs. Erlynne!
units.name: PARKER

units.text: LORD WINDERMERE starts .
MRS. ERLYNNE enters , very beautifully dressed and very dignified .
LADY WINDERMERE clutches at her fan , then lets it drop on the door .
She bows coldly to MRS. ERLYNNE, who bows to her sweetly in turn , and sails into the room .
You have dropped your fan, Lady Windermere.
units.name: LORD DARLINGTON

units.text: Picks it up and hands it to her .
How do you do, again, Lord Windermere? How charming your sweet wife looks! Quite a picture!
units.name: MRS. ERLYNNE

units.text: In a low voice .
It was terribly rash of you to come!
units.name: LORD WINDERMERE

units.text: Smiling .

The wisest thing I ever did in my life. And, by the way, you must pay me a good deal of attention this evening. I am afraid of the women. You must introduce me to some of them. The men I can always manage. How do you do, Lord Augustus? You have quite neglected me lately. I have not seen you since yesterday. I am afraid you’re faithless. Every one told me so.
units.name: MRS. ERLYNNE

units.text: Now really, Mrs. Erlynne, allow me to explain.
units.name: LORD AUGUSTUS

units.text: R.C.
